questions.question: Name the four kinds of motion, define a cam and a follower, and describe what happens to the follower during one turn of the cam.
questions.expected_answer: Rotary (turning in a circle), linear (straight line), reciprocating (back and forth or up and down in a straight line) and oscillating (swinging along an arc). A cam is a specially shaped wheel on a rotating shaft; the follower is a rod held in a guide that rests on the cam's edge. In one turn of the cam the high part pushes the follower up (the rise) and the low part lets it fall back (the fall), so the follower completes one up-and-down cycle: rotary motion becomes reciprocating motion.

questions.question: Describe an eccentric wheel, the kind of motion it gives its follower, and what determines the size of the follower's stroke.
questions.expected_answer: An eccentric wheel is a round disc with its shaft fixed off centre, so the distance from shaft to edge varies around the disc. It gives smooth, even, wave-like reciprocating motion with no jolts, up for half the turn and down for half. The stroke is twice the distance by which the shaft is off centre; the size of the disc does not change it.

questions.question: Compare the snail cam with the eccentric wheel in terms of shape, follower motion and direction of rotation, and give a use for each.
questions.expected_answer: The snail cam is shaped like a snail shell, spiralling outwards to a step; it lifts the follower slowly for most of the turn then lets it drop suddenly, and it can turn in one direction only because backwards the follower jams on the step. Uses: tapping woodpecker toy, stamping or hammer machines, clock striking mechanisms. The eccentric wheel is a plain off-centre disc; it gives smooth equal rise and fall and works turned either way. Uses: nodding toy animals, windmill pump rods.
